_note: Source of truth for projects.html. Edit here, then run: python3 tools/build_projects.py. Badges: PyPI version and pepy downloads come from 'pypi' (set 'pepy': false until pepy.tech lists the package), conda from 'conda', crates.io from 'crate' (only if a Rust crate exists), DOI from 'zenodo' (concept DOI only). A card may use 'images' (a list, stacked) instead of 'image'. 'icon' (optional) is a small square PNG shown beside the card title.

projects.name: pyCoreRelator
projects.label: Python
projects.description: A Python toolkit for pairwise stratigraphic correlation analysis among sediment cores and well-log data.

image.alt: Flowchart of the pyCoreRelator correlation workflow.

projects.citation: Lai, L.S.-H., Sylvester, Z., Covault, J.A., Gomberg, J.S., Nieminski, N.M. (Accepted 2026) Reproducible event-bed correlation with uncertainty: pyCoreRelator. Sedimentology.

projects.name: pyLogCrafter
projects.label: Python
projects.description: Basin-scale well-log quality control, spatial normalization, gap filling, and electrofacies tools.

image.alt: Electrofacies (sandstone, siltstone, carbonate) from 10,438 ML-processed wells in the Delaware Mountain Group, Permian Basin.

projects.name: SubsurfiX
projects.label: Python · Rust
projects.description: SubsurfiX from a folder of well logs to a 3D property model you can simulate on. Log QC, gap filling, well correlation, property modeling, and flow and heat simulation in one Rust engine, run from Python or the command line, with every filled value traceable.

image.alt: 3D porosity model built from 60 Kansas wells.

projects.name: pyLogDigitizer
projects.label: Python
projects.description: pyLogDigitizer turns scanned paper well logs (TIFF) into LAS files, with a local browser app to check and fix every step. Nothing leaves your machine.

image.alt: A scanned paper log traced into a LAS curve.

projects.name: pyBasinSubs
projects.label: Python · R
projects.description: pyBasinSubs reconstructs how a sedimentary basin sank and filled through time by backstripping its layers. It's a new Python package that extends my original R code, BasinSubs (Lai et al., 2021, *Sedimentary Geology*; Lai et al., 2022, *Communications Earth & Environment*), which stays available as its own repo.

projects.name: pyTopoComplexity
projects.label: Python
projects.description: A Python package for multiscale topographic complexity analysis.

image.alt: Wavelet curvature of a digital elevation model.

projects.citation: Lai, L. S.-H., Booth, A. M., Duvall, A. R., and Herzig, E. (2025) Short Communication: Multiscale topographic complexity analysis with pyTopoComplexity. Earth Surface Dynamics, 13(3), 417–435, https://doi.org/10.5194/esurf-13-417-2025

projects.name: pyValleyWidth

projects.description: Measure valley width from a DTM with an elevation-threshold method, built on pytopotoolbox.
